title: Technician can read unassigned incidents
detail:
In router.ts GET /api/incidents/:id handler, the Technician ownership check is: `if (req.user?.role === "Technician" && row.assigneeUserId !== null && row.assigneeUserId !== req.user.id)`. When row.assigneeUserId === null (unassigned incident in OPEN state), the early-out `row.assigneeUserId !== null` skips the check entirely, so any Technician — including unassigned ones — can read any unassigned incident. The intent of Technician-only-mine is to limit Technicians to incidents they're assigned to; unassigned incidents should be excluded too.

Guard: change the check to `if (req.user?.role === "Technician" && row.assigneeUserId !== req.user.id)` so null-vs-undefined mismatch is correctly rejected.

title: P2002 race on notification:critical partial unique index not caught
detail: In incidentStateRepository.ts applyTransition, the optional tx.notification.create({...}) writes a critical notification inside the $transaction. The migration defines a partial unique index Notification_incidentId_severity_active_unique_idx on (incidentId, severity) WHERE acknowledgedAt IS NULL. A concurrent UNSAFE submission collapses to a single Notification row (P2002). The repository doc-comment explicitly says 'the P2002 catch is the caller's responsibility'. The caller in transitionHelpers.ts commitTransition only catches OptimisticConcurrencyError, so a P2002 on the notification write becomes a generic 500 internal_error instead of being treated as a concurrent_modification conflict (409). Guard: in commitTransition, also catch the Prisma P2002 error code and treat it as a concurrent_modification conflict, or move the P2002 catch into applyTransition and re-throw as OptimisticConcurrencyError.

title: writeWarningNotification P2002 race not handled
detail: In rules/applyTransition.ts, the auto-create path now calls writeWarningNotification(tx, ...) inside the $transaction. The writer (per the migration's partial unique index) enforces at-most-one-active-banner per (incidentId, severity). A second auto-create from the same alert-id race (or re-fire after a previous warning was acknowledged-then-resurfaced) yields a P2002 violation. The error propagates out of $transaction, rolling back the entire (Alert + Incident + Notification) commit. The caller (hook) does not appear to catch P2002 specifically. Result: a benign idempotency race becomes a hard transaction rollback and a 500-style failure for the ingest path.

title: Alert FK retrofit migration fails on legacy acknowledgedByUserId values
detail: The migration adds ALTER TABLE "Alert" ADD CONSTRAINT "Alert_acknowledgedByUserId_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("acknowledgedByUserId") REFERENCES "User"("id"). Per the migration comment, Alert.acknowledgedByUserId has been a free String since Story 3.5. If any existing Alert row has a non-null acknowledgedByUserId value that does not match a User.id row, the FK constraint addition fails and the entire forward migration aborts. Guard: in the migration, NULL-out legacy acknowledgedByUserId values that don't have a matching User before adding the FK, or wrap the ALTER in a DO block that pre-cleans orphans.

title: transition() trusts undefined assigneeUserId as INVALID, but empty string slips through
detail: In transitions.ts applyAssign: `if ((from !== "OPEN" && from !== "ACKNOWLEDGED") || assignee === undefined || assignee === null) { return { ok: false, ... } }`. The check rejects undefined and null but allows empty string "". The Zod body schema (assignee_user_id: z.string().uuid()) would catch this upstream, but the pure state machine has no defense-in-depth. Guard: also reject falsy strings.

title: buildIncidentPayload accepts arbitrary severity string
detail: In rules/incidentFromAlert.ts buildIncidentPayload, the input.severity passes through directly. The Prisma Incident.severity column is a free-form String (per the schema comment). If a future RuleSeverity literal appears before the wire-boundary validation is updated, the Incident row commits with an unknown severity that the IncidentSeveritySchema cannot parse on read. The downstream incidentRowToPayload then casts via row.severity as IncidentPayload["severity"] — bypassing type safety. Guard: validate input.severity against the closed set at the top of buildIncidentPayload and throw on unknown values.

title: incident:opened emit skipped silently on schema parse failure
detail: In rules/applyTransition.ts the parsedIncident.safeParse failure path only logs console.warn; the Story 4.4 detail page listener never receives the event and there's no operator-facing observability beyond the console.warn. Guard: surface a metric/audit event when the schema parse fails, or fall back to emitting a minimal payload.

title: commitTransition throws on P2002 from applyTransition becomes 500
detail: transitionHelpers.ts commitTransition wraps applyTransition in try/catch that only catches OptimisticConcurrencyError. applyTransition can throw any Prisma error — including P2002 (race on partial unique index for the notification:critical write), P2003 (FK violation if a User was deleted between request validation and write), or transient connection errors. Only the OptimisticConcurrencyError sentinel is mapped to 409; all others become 500. The caller cannot distinguish a benign race (P2002) from a real outage.

title: seedUsers createdFresh heuristic is unreliable under fast re-seed
detail: seedUsers.ts uses a 5-second threshold to classify inserts vs no-ops. On a slow DB or under clock skew, a freshly-upserted row's createdAt can be >5s old by the time the SELECT returns, misclassifying it as a no-op. Conversely, on a fast re-run within 5s, an existing row's createdAt may still be 'fresh enough' to be misclassified. The counter is purely diagnostic but misleading.

title: buildTransitionHandler runs RBAC at middleware layer only — no defense-in-depth in handler
detail: The route layer in router.ts uses authorize({ action: ..., resource: 'Incident' }, deps.audit) middleware. If the middleware is misconfigured or replaced in a future refactor, the handlers themselves don't re-check the role. Compare to the inline Technician-only-mine check, which IS in the handler body.

title: loadOrRespond doesn't enforce Technician ownership at read time
detail: transitionHelpers.ts loadOrRespond returns the row unconditionally for any caller that reaches it. The GET /api/incidents/:id handler in router.ts DOES enforce Technician-only-mine, but the loadOrRespond helper itself has no such guard. If a future verb reuses loadOrRespond, the ownership check is bypassed unless the caller re-implements it.
